description: Authentication, authorization, and client lifecycle: NextAuth v5 Credentials/JWT, src/proxy.ts (NOT middleware.ts — Next 16 renamed the convention, see node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/proxy.md) role-gating /admin/* and /app/*, login page with role-based redirect, accountant-only client invitation flow (POST /api/admin/clients + /admin/clients UI), console EmailService stub, public /activate/[token] activation page, and accountantId-scoped Category CRUD. Depends on FEAT-001 (schema + seeded accountant). Every API route re-checks authorization server-side, never trusting proxy.ts alone.
steps: Create src/auth.ts following the next-auth v5 beta pattern from the reference app (c:\Users\GermanDarioArbelaez\Documents\project-agent\expense-tracker-ocr\src\auth.ts) but extended: Credentials provider's authorize() looks up User by email, bcryptjs.compare against user.password, and on success returns { id, email, name, role, locale } plus — for CLIENT role — the ClientProfile.status and ClientProfile.id (join via prisma.user.findUnique({ include: { clientProfile: true } })). jwt callback copies role, clientStatus, clientProfileId onto the token; session callback copies them onto session.user. session strategy 'jwt'. pages.signIn = '/login'. Secret from AUTH_SECRET.

Create src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts (or the exact NextAuth v5 route convention — confirm via next-auth package.json exports, which show handlers exported from the root auth.ts) exporting { GET, POST } = handlers from '@/auth'.

Create src/proxy.ts (the Next 16 convention replacing middleware.ts) wrapping `auth()`: redirect unauthenticated requests to /login; for paths under /admin, require role === 'ACCOUNTANT'; for paths under /app, require role === 'CLIENT' AND clientStatus === 'ACTIVE' (redirect INVITED/SUSPENDED clients to a 'pending activation' or 'suspended' notice page, not into the app). Export `config = { matcher: ['/admin/:path*', '/app/:path*'] }`. Add a short code comment citing that this file replaces middleware.ts per Next 16's AGENTS.md-mandated doc read.

Create src/app/login/page.tsx: a Client Component form posting email/password via next-auth's signIn('credentials', {redirect: false}) (or a Server Action calling signIn), then client-side redirect based on session role (ACCOUNTANT -> /admin, CLIENT -> /app). Minimal styling consistent with the project's Tailwind v4 setup (globals.css already present).

Create src/lib/email.ts: an EmailService interface (e.g. `sendInvitation(to, activationUrl): Promise<void>`) and a ConsoleEmailService implementing it by console.log-ing the activation link; export the active implementation (console stub for now, with a comment on how a real provider — tentatively Resend per RESEND_API_KEY — would be swapped in later without changing callers).

Create POST /api/admin/clients (src/app/api/admin/clients/route.ts): require `const session = await auth()` and session.user.role === 'ACCOUNTANT' (403 otherwise, this is the real server-side check — proxy.ts is not sufficient per the task's CRITICAL requirement). Accepts businessName/email/name (+ optional kvkNumber/btwNumber), creates a CLIENT User (role CLIENT, a locked/unusable placeholder password hash since the client hasn't set one yet — e.g. bcryptjs.hash of a random token) + ClientProfile (status INVITED, accountantId = session.user.id), generates a random 32-byte token, stores only its SHA-256 hex hash in InvitationToken (expiresAt = now + 48h), and calls EmailService.sendInvitation with a URL embedding the RAW (unhashed) token (/activate/<token>). Also add GET /api/admin/clients listing the accountant's own clients with their status (scoped by accountantId — never return other accountants' clients).
Create src/app/admin/clients/page.tsx: Server Component (or Client Component fetching the API) showing the invite form and the list of this accountant's clients with status badges.

Create GET /api/activate/[token]/route.ts or a Server Component directly in src/app/activate/[token]/page.tsx that validates the token: hash the incoming raw token with SHA-256, look up InvitationToken by tokenHash, check usedAt is null and expiresAt > now, else show an 'invalid or expired' state. On valid token, show a form to set a password.

Create POST /api/activate/[token]/route.ts: re-validate the token (same checks, server-side, race-safe via a transaction), hash the new password with bcryptjs, update the User's password, set ClientProfile.status = ACTIVE, set InvitationToken.usedAt = now — all in a single prisma.$transaction so a token can't be double-used by a race. Reject with a clear error if the token is already used or expired.

Create Category CRUD under src/app/api/categories/route.ts (GET list, POST create) and src/app/api/categories/[id]/route.ts (PATCH, DELETE): every handler calls `auth()`, and for ACCOUNTANT requires the category's accountantId === session.user.id (for POST, force accountantId = session.user.id, ignore any client-supplied value); CLIENT role gets read-only GET scoped to their own accountant's categories (via their ClientProfile.accountantId), never write access. Return 403 on any violation.
Create a minimal src/app/admin/categories/page.tsx (or reuse an existing admin layout) for the accountant to manage categories via the API above.

Run `npx prisma generate` if any schema change was needed for clientStatus/role lookups (should not be, FEAT-001 already covers this), then `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, and a short-lived `npm run start` + curl smoke test of /api/admin/clients (expect 401/403 without a session cookie) and /api/health (expect 200), then kill the server.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthenticated requests to /admin/* and /app/* are redirected to /login by src/proxy.ts
POST /api/admin/clients as a non-ACCOUNTANT (or unauthenticated) session returns 401/403, verified by a direct curl/script call bypassing the UI

A freshly created invitation's raw token successfully activates the account exactly once; a second activation attempt with the same token fails with a clear error (verified via a small script using Date mocking or a manually expired expiresAt row, not real 48h waiting)

An invitation token with expiresAt in the past is rejected by the activation route even if otherwise valid (verified by inserting a row with a past expiresAt via a script and calling the activation API)
Category POST/PATCH/DELETE from a CLIENT session or from an ACCOUNTANT session targeting another accountant's category returns 403
`npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and `npm run build` all pass
verification: `npm run build` — succeeds and lists /login, /admin/clients, /activate/[token], /api/admin/clients, /api/categories among the routes
Short-lived `npm run start` + curl: GET /api/admin/clients without a session cookie returns 401; curl /api/health returns 200; then kill the server, confirm no process left running

A one-off script (e.g. scripts/verify-invitation.ts, deleted or documented afterward) that: creates an accountant + client + invitation token directly via Prisma, calls the activation logic (either via the route's exported handler function or by importing the same validation helper used by the route) twice with the same token and asserts the second call fails, and once more with a manually expired token and asserts failure — prints PASS/FAIL for each case
findings: Session shape (src/types/next-auth.d.ts + src/auth.ts): session.user has {id, email, name, role: 'ACCOUNTANT'|'CLIENT', locale, clientStatus: 'INVITED'|'ACTIVE'|'SUSPENDED'|null, clientProfileId: string|null}. clientStatus/clientProfileId are null for ACCOUNTANT sessions. Get it server-side via `const session = await auth()` from '@/auth' (never trust src/proxy.ts alone — every route re-checks session.user.role/ownership itself). IMPORTANT typing gotcha: next-auth v5.0.0-beta.30's 'next-auth' and 'next-auth/jwt' entry points only re-export types from '@auth/core' — module augmentation for custom Session/User/JWT fields MUST target `declare module '@auth/core/types'` and `declare module '@auth/core/jwt'`, NOT 'next-auth'/'next-auth/jwt' (those don't merge). Also required: `trustHost: true` in the NextAuth config (src/auth.ts) — without it, `next start` throws [auth][error] UntrustedHost on every /api/auth/* call because Auth.js only trusts the Host header by default on Vercel/Cloudflare Pages or outside production; this app is self-hosted so it must opt in explicitly. Route paths for FEAT-003/004/005: GET/POST /api/categories (role-scoped: ACCOUNTANT gets own categories + write, CLIENT gets read-only via their ClientProfile.accountantId), PATCH/DELETE /api/categories/[id] (ACCOUNTANT-only, ownership-checked), GET/POST /api/admin/clients (ACCOUNTANT-only), GET/POST /api/activate/[token] (public), /api/auth/[...nextauth] (NextAuth handlers). src/proxy.ts (NOT middleware.ts) gates /admin/:path* (role===ACCOUNTANT) and /app/:path* (role===CLIENT && clientStatus==='ACTIVE', else redirect to /estado-cuenta); unauthenticated anywhere under those -> /login. EmailService interface (src/lib/email.ts): `interface EmailService { sendInvitation(to: string, activationUrl: string): Promise<void> }`, active implementation exported as `emailService` (currently ConsoleEmailService doing console.log — swap the exported instance for a Resend-backed implementation later without touching callers). Activation/invitation logic lives in src/lib/activation.ts (hashToken, findValidInvitation, activateInvitation) and is shared by the route handler and scripts/verify-invitation.ts — reuse activateInvitation's transaction pattern (prisma.$transaction with a conditional updateMany on usedAt:null) as the race-safe single-use template for any other token-based flow. Category writes always force accountantId = session.user.id server-side, ignoring any client-supplied value. Verified: `npx prisma generate` clean; npm run lint 0 errors (user-run, after fixing two react-hooks/set-state-in-effect violations in admin/clients and admin/categories pages by moving the fetch-on-mount into an inline async function per-effect instead of a useCallback dependency); npx tsc --noEmit 0 errors (user-run); npm run build succeeded listing /, /login, /admin, /admin/clients, /admin/categories, /activate/[token], /estado-cuenta, /app, /api/activate/[token], /api/admin/clients, /api/auth/[...nextauth], /api/categories, /api/categories/[id], /api/health, plus 'ƒ Proxy (Middleware)' confirming proxy.ts (not middleware.ts) is active (user-run); scripts/verify-invitation.ts (left in place, documented here rather than deleted, per context.json's guidance to keep ad-hoc DB verification scripts) printed 3/3 PASS: valid token activates once, second attempt with same token rejected as already_used, expired token rejected as invalid_or_expired (user-run via npx tsx); runtime smoke test via user-run `npm run start` + curl: GET /api/auth/session -> 200 with null session and auth cookies set (no UntrustedHost error after adding trustHost:true), GET /api/admin/clients without a session cookie -> 401 {"error":"No autorizado"}, GET /api/health -> 200 {"status":"ok","database":"connected"}; server stopped afterward, no process left running. All of this FEAT's own bash/tsc/build/lint/start/curl verification had to be run manually by the user and results relayed back, since this agent's own terminal tool hit the environment's known 130/^C blocking issue noted in context.json.
